history.summary: Fixed both iteration-7 review findings in internal/docsguard, test/docs-only. (1) Sentence-scoped context: added enclosingSentence (bounds a block of text to the sentence containing a given match, split on .!?) and changed recommendationMention to check affirmative deprecation context against each candidate recommendation match's own enclosing sentence, instead of the whole paragraph once. An unrelated deprecation-context word about a different subject, in an earlier or later sentence of the same paragraph, no longer suppresses a live recommendation elsewhere in it. (2) Directly-governed negation: tightened hasAffirmativeDeprecationContext's negation association to require the negation word/phrase within negationProximityWords (3) words of the deprecation-context word it must directly govern, and added negationBoundaryPattern (semicolon, em/en dash, or double hyphen) as a hard stop a negation word cannot be read across. 'Do not use the api_key parameter; it is deprecated' no longer misreads the leading not (which governs use) as negating deprecated, since the semicolon separates them; 'is not actually deprecated' still correctly negates, since not directly and closely precedes deprecated with no boundary between them. Added TestScanTextContextIsSentenceScopedNotParagraphWide (unrelated-subject context in a different sentence does not suppress, including a wrapped variant; genuine same-sentence context still does) and TestScanTextNegationMustDirectlyGovernDeprecationWord (several do-not-use-it-is-deprecated phrasings, including a -- dash variant and wrapped forms, do not violate; a negation that directly governs deprecated itself still violates). history.commit_title: fix(docs): [B] scope deprecation to recommendation clause
history.summary: Fixed the iteration-9 review finding in internal/docsguard, test/docs-only. Added adversativeBoundaryPattern (but/however/yet/though/although/nevertheless/nonetheless/whereas) and changed hasAffirmativeDeprecationContext to take the recommendation match's own position, checking for each candidate context match whether one of these connectors sits between the two, in either direction; a connector in between means the context describes a different, contrasting clause and does not qualify the recommendation. Semicolons and em/en dashes were deliberately NOT added to this pattern, since every existing fixture using one ('Do not use the api_key query parameter; it is deprecated.') is an elaboration of the very thing just recommended, not a contrast, and must continue to suppress. hasAffirmativeDeprecationContext's table-row and recommendation-prose callers were updated to pass the recommendation's position (len(line) for table rows, preserving prior whole-row behavior unchanged). Rewrote internal/docsguard from a hand-written regex/heuristic pseudo-Markdown scanner to a real CommonMark+GFM AST-based scanner, as the root-cause fix the final reviews required. Dependency decision: added github.com/yuin/goldmark/v2 v2.1.6 (0 known vulnerabilities per check_dependency_vulnerabilities) as the sole new direct dependency. Need: a real, spec-correct Markdown parser is the only reliable way to flatten rendered inline text (links, raw HTML/comments, emphasis/strong/strikethrough, nested combinations) and to apply CommonMark's exact code-span/fenced-code/list-continuation rules; Go's regexp (RE2) has no backreferences, so 'closing delimiter run of the same length as the opening run' cannot even be expressed as one regex, which is why the iteration-12 approach had hit a hard ceiling. Alternative considered: continuing to extend the bounded regex heuristics (the orchestrator's instruction given this history across iterations 11-12) -- rejected per this iteration's explicit direction, and because each prior fix successfully closed its specific case but kept reopening new ones, confirming the approach cannot be made complete. Security impact: parsing is read-only and local (no network, no code execution, no templating); goldmark v2 is actively maintained with no open advisories. Maintenance impact: one pinned, deterministic dependency with a clean `go mod tidy` diff, replacing roughly 500 lines of increasingly complex hand-rolled pattern logic with a spec-conformant parser; goldmark v2's text.Decoder design (code spans/raw HTML bound to an IdentityDecoder, regular text decoded via the full HTML5 entity table) gives the exact semantics needed without any extra decode logic in this package. Implementation: docsguard.go (ScanText parses via a shared parser.New(parser.WithExtensions(extension.GFMParser)) instance and walks the AST, with an explicit max-line-length fail-closed guard and a recover() around the walk so any parser panic or internal error fails closed rather than silently passing); scan.go (flattenInline recursively flattens Text/CodeSpan/RawHTML/AutoLink per real CommonMark rendering semantics -- this single function is what makes links/HTML/comments/emphasis 'just work' via real parsing instead of regex splitting; flattenInlineByLine preserves per-line credential precision across wrapped paragraphs; scanCodeBlock/scanTableCell/scanProseBlock dispatch per block kind); credential.go (hasParameterCredential/rawAuthorization ported, now operating on flattened text); context.go (all prior negation/adversative/sentence/clause-scoping logic ported, plus two new mechanisms: a bare-version-requires-construction-word check, and transport-specific context binding via transportKindNear/nearestAPIKeyOccurrence so a deprecation notice about one transport cannot suppress a recommendation of a different one). Verified against real shipped documentation end-to-end and fixed two genuine issues the new, more thorough scanning surfaced: a coincidental false-positive match in docs/API_KEY_VERIFIER.md's unrelated historical database-query prose (wording changed 'accepted' -> 'validated', meaning preserved) and a real panic from an off-by-one in the recommendation-match proximity window (weakRecommendationVerbPattern tightened from use\w* to explicit use|uses|used|using to stop it incidentally matching the noun 'user'; defensive index clamping added throughout the context-scoping arithmetic). Debugged and fixed two parser-interaction bugs surfaced by new adversarial regression tests added this iteration: nearestAPIKeyOccurrence was measuring distance in raw bytes while its sibling proximity check measured in words, which could make the two disagree about which api_key mention a context word actually describes and silently misclassify its transport -- fixed by unifying both on word-distance; and the transport-word-matching window (40 chars either side) was wide enough to catch two different transport words from two different api_key mentions in the same short sentence, making the classification wrongly ambiguous -- narrowed to 20 chars. Added three new adversarial regression test functions: TestScanTextBareVersionRequiresConstruction, TestScanTextTransportMismatchDoesNotSuppress, and TestScanTextStructuralParsingCorrectness, covering every required case (transport-specific binding across form/query/raw/response-field, bare-version non-affirmation, variable-length code-span delimiters, multi-line code-span content normalization, short/unclosed fences, list-continuation vs indented code). Rewrote TestScanTextRenderedMarkupSplit: smoke-testing the real parser disproved iteration-12's premise that single-punctuation-character emphasis/strong/strikethrough wrapping (api*_*key, Authorization_:_, api~_~key) renders as a split anchor -- real CommonMark flanking rules leave these as literal text -- so those cases moved from positive to negative fixtures with corrected comments, and new positive cases were added for genuine splitting vectors (HTML comments, Markdown links, nested tag+link/tag+entity combinations, whole-word strong emphasis). All prior fixtures (iterations 1-12) updated only where they depended on bare single-row table syntax (now real two-row GFM tables) or a bare 0.13.0 with no construction word (now paired with an explicit removal/deprecated word), and otherwise pass unchanged. docsguard gate re-run against all shipped Markdown: 0 violations across 28 files. Final reviews of the iteration-13 structured (goldmark v2 AST) rewrite found three remaining root-cause gaps within that same structured design, rather than a need for further ad-hoc patching. (1) SECURITY MEDIUM 10/10 + code: ast.HTMLBlock was not walked at all, so a raw HTML block's visible rendered content (a
,

, or 

 containing a credential or recommendation) was never scanned, while comments, tag/attribute markup, and script/style content needed to stay correctly excluded as non-visible, with malformed HTML handled conservatively/fail-closed and diagnostics still redacted. (2) Soft-wrapped raw Authorization detection: an ordinary Markdown soft line break between the header name and its value ('Authorization:\nTOKEN', which renders as a single space) was not detected, because credential scanning ran per physical line only; it needed to also scan the fully rendered/flattened block text, retaining a precise contributing line range, correct code/hard-break semantics, correctness for ordinary multi-line query/form examples, and no duplicate diagnostics or false merging across unrelated block/cell boundaries. (3) Compact mixed transport: the symmetric, flat character-window transport-word binding (transportKindNear) could not correctly classify a compact sentence naming two transports close together with no anchor word ('api_key form deprecated; use api_key query' must violate), and -- more importantly -- treated a genuinely ambiguous classification the same as 'no information available', letting it default to suppression instead of failing safe; it needed to be replaced with directional, occurrence-specific binding, with an ambiguous classification on either side never suppressing, while preserving natural variants and prior accepted warnings. Fixed all three remaining structured-parser gaps from the final review of iteration 13, within the existing goldmark v2 AST design (no dependency change; go.mod/go.sum untouched). (1) HTML blocks: added internal/docsguard/html.go. flattenHTMLBlockText is a small, linear state machine recognizing exactly the handful of constructs CommonMark's own HTML-block grammar defines -- comments, CDATA sections, processing instructions, declarations, tag markup/attributes (all dropped, none ever visible), and <script>/<style> content specifically (dropped too, since neither ever displays as readable prose) -- while keeping everything else, including a <div>'s or <pre>'s inner text, as visible text to scan exactly like a paragraph's. An unterminated comment/CDATA/PI/declaration is handled the way a real browser's tokenizer does (the rest of the block is still never visible, so it is still dropped), but anything this state machine cannot otherwise confidently classify -- an unterminated tag, or an unterminated <script>/<style> element -- fails closed the other way: scanning falls back to treating it as ordinary visible text, rather than risking silently hiding a real credential behind a malformed document. Wired *ast.HTMLBlock into ScanText's walk dispatch (scanHTMLBlock), reusing the existing credential-match-span and recommendationMention checks with line attribution via a byte-offset map back into source. (2) Soft-wrapped Authorization: refactored rawAuthorization/hasParameterCredential (credential.go) to expose match-span variants (rawAuthorizationMatches/parameterCredentialMatches) alongside their existing boolean forms. scanInlineCredentials (scan.go) now checks a raw Authorization header example over the whole block's joined, per-run text (joinRunsWithOffsets), so a header name and its value separated only by an ordinary Markdown soft or hard line break are still read together exactly as they render, with each match mapped back to its own precise, contributing [StartLine, EndLine] -- while this is the only pass performed over the joined text (an unwrapped single-line header is still reported exactly once, not twice, and two separate blocks are never joined together, since this always operates within one AST block's own runs). Parameter-credential matching stays per physical line, unchanged, since that case does not need this. (3) Compact mixed transport: replaced transportKindNear's flat +/-20-character symmetric window with directional, occurrence-specific word-distance binding -- the transport word, among every occurrence of every kind within the proximity bound, nearest to the specific api_key mention in either direction -- and changed its return contract to distinguish a genuine tie between two different kinds (ambiguous=true) from simply no transport word being nearby at all (ambiguous=false, kind=""). hasAffirmativeDeprecationContext now treats an ambiguous classification on either side as failing safe: it never suppresses, unlike the prior design, which let an ambiguous ('') classification on the context side fall through to the same suppressing branch as 'no information', the concrete bug the review identified. Added TestScanTextHTMLBlockVisibleText, TestScanTextSoftWrappedRawAuthorization, and TestScanTextCompactMixedTransportDirectional covering every reviewer example (including the exact compact phrasing and a constructed genuine-tie adversarial case demonstrating the old code's suppression bug is now fixed) plus block/multi-line/table/HTML positive and negative fixtures.
